name: Sheet Pan Smoked Sausage, Broccoli, and Cheddar

ingredients.buy: 28 cups broccoli florets (about 5 1/4 lb, 8 medium heads)
3 lb andouille smoked sausage, sliced into rounds (about three and a half 14 oz ropes)
3 1/2 cups shredded cheddar, added the last 2 minutes

prose.intro_html: Most weeknight dinners that come off one pan lean on a starch to fill the plate, and that starch is usually the cheapest, emptiest thing in the cart. This one skips it entirely. Sliced andouille smoked sausage and fresh broccoli florets go on the sheet pan together, and as the sausage roasts it renders its own fat right down over the broccoli, so the florets caramelize instead of steam. A handful of sharp cheddar over the top in the last couple of minutes ties it together. No oil to buy, no rice, no potatoes, just three things that roast into a real dinner. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 15 grams of carbs. That is a full sheet pan of dinner working for your body and your wallet at the same time.
shop_smart: The sausage is the anchor, so buy the rope. You want three pounds of andouille smoked sausage, which is about three and a half of the standard fourteen ounce ropes. A pork rope slices into rounds that brown with real color and give up enough of their own fat to cook the broccoli, so you are not buying oil on top of it. Andouille brings a little Cajun heat; a plain smoked rope works the same way if that is what is on the shelf.

Fresh broccoli, about eight medium heads. Roughly five and a quarter pounds, bought as whole heads and cut down into florets at home, about twenty-eight cups all told. It has to be fresh, not frozen: fresh florets roast and caramelize at the edges where frozen ones just weep water and steam. This is the vegetable doing the work a pile of rice or potatoes usually does.

Cheddar is the finish, so buy enough for a good blanket. Three and a half cups of shredded cheddar goes on for just the last minute or two, long enough to melt and pull everything together. Shredded off a block or straight from the bag both melt fine here; the sharp stuff pays you back in more flavor.

Salt and pepper are the only seasoning this needs. The sausage and the roasted cheddar carry the flavor, so all you add at the end is salt and pepper to taste. Those are staples you already own, which is part of why a pan this simple lands so cheap.
make_it: Weigh a large empty mixing bowl and write the number down. Sheet-pan food comes off loose, so this is how you will split the batch into 14 even servings by weight at the end instead of eyeballing every container.
Heat the oven to 400 degrees F. Line two large sheet pans with foil or parchment for easy cleanup. Slice the smoked sausage into rounds and cut the broccoli into bite-sized florets.

Spread the broccoli and sausage across the two pans in a single layer, splitting them evenly. A 14-serving batch will not fit on one pan, and crowding is what makes broccoli steam instead of roast. Roast for 15 minutes.
Pull the pans and flip the sausage and toss the broccoli so the other side colors. Roast another 5 to 10 minutes, until the broccoli is as tender as you like it and the edges have caramelized.
Scatter the shredded cheddar over both pans and return them to the oven for 1 to 2 minutes, just until the cheese melts. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Tip everything into the mixing bowl you weighed in Step 1. Weigh it full, subtract the empty weight to get the cooked total, divide by 14, and scoop that exact weight into each container.
prose.portion_html: Tip all the roasted sausage, broccoli, and melted cheddar into the bowl you weighed in Step 1, then subtract that empty weight to get the cooked total. Divide by 14 and scoop that exact weight into each container. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
prose.cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a full sheet pan of roasted sausage and broccoli under melted cheddar. The sausage and the cheese carry the flavor and the protein; the broccoli does the job the rice or the potatoes used to, with none of the carbs and none of the cost.

steps: Weigh a large empty mixing bowl and note the number for portioning later.
Heat the oven to 400 degrees F, line two sheet pans, slice the sausage into rounds, and cut the broccoli into florets.
Spread the broccoli and sausage across the two pans in a single layer and roast 15 minutes.
Flip the sausage and toss the broccoli, then roast another 5 to 10 minutes until the broccoli caramelizes.
Scatter the cheddar over both pans and roast 1 to 2 minutes until melted, then season with salt and pepper.
Tip everything into the weighed bowl, subtract the empty weight, and divide the total across 14 containers.
